correctness.rationale: The lattice is covolume one, so an independent Haar displacement is uniform in its Euclidean Voronoi cell. Complete sign-case decomposition establishes the six sufficient Voronoi halfspaces. Solving their intersections yields six equal-radius vertices for every 0<delta<1/2 and the square at zero. The circumdisk minus disjoint circular caps gives the exact entire radial CDF. Its diameter derivative vanishes and the second derivative equals -4 times the sum of side-distance over corner-height ratios, yielding exactly C_delta=2(1/delta+1/(1-delta)+1/(1-delta+delta^2)) and square C_0=4. The third cap activates in a delta^2 window and its angle divided by delta has the explicit limit sqrt((1-2 sqrt(2)t)_+), whereas the first two cap angles change by O(delta^2). Bounded convergence proves the delta^3 boundary-layer formula. Independent angular integration, geometric polygon checks, exact ratios and numerical scaling tests corroborate the analytic proof; finite tests are not its basis.

value.rationale: The intrinsic near-diameter probability on a flat two-torus is a natural population-level shape invariant. The theorem computes its sharp tail coefficient for a complete one-parameter shear family, displays its discontinuous divergence at the rectangular lattice, and analytically resolves the transition by a new nontrivial delta^2-radius / delta^3-probability scaling function with a distinguished threshold t=1/(2 sqrt 2). This explains a genuine lack of uniform endpoint stability under smooth geometric perturbations. These are structural asymptotics not an arbitrary finite numerical slice or a simple reformulation of the pre-existing qualitative inverse theorem.
